text:
maria: Handoff — I'm handing over the ongoing prefetch-oscillation alerts. Root cause still under investigation but symptoms are: sudden enqueue/consume imbalance on prefetch-workers causing long tail latency and token-generation timeouts for a subset of customer requests. Currently active alerts: prefetch-queue-depth-High, prefetch-consumer-lag, prefetch-worker-CPU-90.

incident-bot: Pager: prefetch-oscillation (sev3) — triggered 2851234500 — alerting eng-oncall.

maria: TL;DR for next shift: primary = jonas (you pick up paging), secondary = sam (backup + escalation), debbie is covering customer comms if we need to notify customers. I'm staying around for 10 more mins for context handoff.

jonas: taking primary. quick question — any customer-facing error rates yet?

maria: small blip to a handful of customers — 503s up from 0.02% to 0.35% in last 20m for the prefetch path. No broad outage. No CS tickets yet.

maria: Mitigations already in flight:
- scaled prefetch-workers ASG +2 instances at 2851234620
- reduced prefetch concurrency to 8 from 16 for new pods (see rollout in the autoscaler job)
- applied temporary routing rule to send <10% traffic to fallback-prefetch-1 (lower memory version)

sam: noted. are KV cache evictions spiking?

maria: yes, KV eviction rate doubled. likely working set growth for a bad prompt pattern from a customer. I dumped a few heap stats and the consumer logs. snippet below:

```
[2026-03-15T02:07:12Z] prefetch-worker-7 WARN kv_cache_evict key_count=120034 evict_rate=0.23
[2026-03-15T02:08:05Z] prefetch-consumer-2 ERROR consume_timeout id=abc123 duration_ms=120042
[2026-03-15T02:09:40Z] autoscaler INFO scale_up from=6 to=8 reason=queue_depth>800
```

debbie: tagging PS team? we should be ready to send a proactive note if rate doesn't improve in 30m.

maria: yes flagged platform-ps and the partner manager. runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/prefetch-oscillation — follow the 'queue-surge' section. Key runbook steps we've done: scale, reduce concurrency, route small % to fallback. Next recommendations in runbook: enable cache-only mode for prefetch clients, and increase prefetch TTL to reduce churn.

jonas: I'll try cache-only toggle first. How do I flip it safely?

maria: feature-flag in LaunchDarkly: prefetch_cache_only. Toggle → gradual 10% -> 50% -> 100% using the UI. We used 10% in canary already for fallback route.

jonas: doing 10% now.

ops-bot: ACTION: feature_toggle applied by jonas at 2851234740 — prefetch_cache_only=10% for service/prefetch.

jonas: can confirm metrics: queue depth dropped ~12% in last 60s. latency P95 reduced by ~180ms. continuing to 50% in 5m if stable.

maria: good. other parallel action: prefetch worker logs point to a burst of requests from customer org org-4472 hitting very long context. Sam, can you pull the top callers for last 30m and see if we can rate-limit on API key?

sam: grabbing top callers now — running query.

sam: top callers: org-4472 (~42% of prefetch requests), org-1199 (~11%), rest distributed. org-4472 has two jobs that started a batch burst at 02:05Z.

maria: recommend throttling org-4472 to 50rps for prefetch path as temporary mitigation. Runbook suggests per-tenant rate-limit as safe.

jonas: applied tenant throttle for org-4472 via rate-limiter config:
```
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: rate.limits/v1
kind: RateLimit
metadata:
  name: throttle-org-4472
spec:
  tenant: org-4472
  max_rps: 50
EOF
```

ops-bot: CONFIG_CHANGE: rate-limiter updated by jonas at 2851234805 — throttle-org-4472 max_rps=50.

sam: after throttle, org-4472 traffic dropped ~60% in prefetch stream, queue depth further decreased. Good signal.

debbie: I'm drafting a short customer note to org-4472 support contact to explain we observed abnormal batch traffic and applied a temporary throttle; will coordinate tone after you sign off.

maria: sign off. keep it minimal: describe observed spike, mitigation, ask them to adjust job cadence.

jonas: a few operational notes for the new shift:
- primary (jonas): monitor alert set {prefetch-queue-depth-High, prefetch-consumer-lag, prefetch-worker-CPU-90} and paging. If p95 latency worsens by >200ms after toggles, escalate to oncall-sre and ping debbie.
- secondary (sam): own rollback path: if cache-only + throttle do not stabilize within 20m, flip routing to fallback-prefetch-1=50% and open quick rollback PR for recent prefetch consumer change (PR #4221).
- runbook pointer: section 'escalate-to-sre' on the runbook.

sam: noted. also pointing out a coverage gap: after midnight we have only one on-call infra engineer; if this goes sev2 we'll need to pull someone from eng-runtime. debbie, can you ping runtime on rotation?

debbie: will ping runtime and pm-runtime for standby.

maria: outstanding tasks assigned:
- jonas: continue primary, progressive increase prefetch_cache_only to 50% if metrics stable (check in 10m) — DONE 10% now.
- sam: verify PR #4221 health check and stand by for rollback.
- debbie: customer comms, runtime stand-by.
- maria: staying available for 10m then hands off.

jonas: 10m check: metrics look stable. increasing to 50% now.

ops-bot: FEATURE_UPDATE: prefetch_cache_only increased to 50% by jonas at 2851234880.

jonas: 50% in effect — queue depth continues to trend down. alerts are still present but no new escalations.

debbie: drafted note for org-4472 — sending now.

maria: ok I'm stepping out. jonas you're primary. sam secondary. debbie handle comms. If anything degrades, page as usual and escalate. Signing off — maria :wave:

jonas: taking over. I'll post a short summary in the incident tracker and close this handoff thread once we reach stable for 30m.

sam: standby. ping me if p95 > baseline+200ms.

incident-bot: Reminder: follow post-incident checklist in runbook after stabilization — add timeline + mitigations.

jonas: copied. will update the tracker and handback in ~30m or earlier if resolved.

debbie: adding a note in the customer comms channel with the message we agreed on.

maria: thanks all.
